items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: He had a, Claiborne Williams had a fine band, really a fine band. But I was blowing so much horn in them times that his band didn't count too much.

ctx.x: Well, who won these contests? Let me tell you, what about Claiborne Williams and all that? How'd you come out?

He had a, Claiborne Williams had a fine band, really a fine band. But I was blowing so much horn in them times that his band didn't count too much. I was breaking up the house, and where I went, I was tearing up out there. I was young, and I liked it to play, and could play, and I just went on to up everything. All I wanted was a piano and a drum behind me. I didn't need nothing else. I was playing. I was playing. And, uh...
People liked what? What did they want you to play? What would you win the contest with? Anything.

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: Well, there was the three leading orchestras outside of New Orleans. It was Bud Scott, Claiborne William, and Tut Johnson... Well, they was doing all the business out there, and I was with Tut.

ctx.x: He'd sing a lot of waltzes. And then there was time waltzes was awful popular.

And he'd sing a lot of them. Did a lot of singing. But he didn't play anything. Oh, he had a playhouse in his yard, though. That thing was around 12 by 12 was a little girl. He had a real funny to play. He was a great guy. He was a great guy. for his little girl. They had real furniture in there too, but that was just the playhouse there. He had a wonderful home over there. Well, there was the three leading orchestras outside of New Orleans. It was Bud Scott, Claiborne William, and Tut Johnson. Claiborne William…

items.title: John Handy Interview, 1958-12-04
items.q: what's his name, William there, or Donaldsonville, Claiborne Weave.

ctx.x: And then I went by World Iron. I got about $75 of all of us music. Rehearsing that, we got it down. And we had a contest with, what's his name, William there, or Donaldsonville, Claiborne Weave. And we had a contest with, up at Pelican. We had so many people in there, you couldn't get nobody else in the place. They would line it out all on the side, all around the building they would line it, but you couldn't get nobody else in there. Then the next contest we had was the-
